intended_object: The pointwise tensor product F ⊗ G of two functors F, G : C ⥤ D into a monoidal category D, with (F ⊗ G)(X) = F(X) ⊗ G(X) and (F ⊗ G)(f) = F(f) ⊗ G(f). It is the tensor of objects in the pointwise monoidal structure on the functor category. Inferred from the docstring and from its use in functorCategoryMonoidal.
explanation: The body sets obj X := F.obj X ⊗ G.obj X and map f := F.map f ⊗ₘ G.map f, which is exactly the pointwise tensor product of functors. The functor laws are discharged automatically (by aesop_cat) from the fact that tensoring morphisms preserves identities and composition. The hypotheses are the minimal ones the construction needs: C is any category and D is any monoidal category. So the definition matches the intended object at its natural generality.
